note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Aug 31 - Sep 28, 2026, catching up a five-week refresh gap). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: The ten-mile Burlington Wildways Trail is finally finished after nearly a decade of work, linking the Intervale, the Ethan Allen Homestead, Ethan Allen Park and Rock Point in one continuous route from the Winooski River to Lake Champlain. Which stretch would you walk first?

Free apps like Merlin Bird ID and eBird have pulled enough young Vermonters into birdwatching that UVM's ornithology class has doubled to around 60 students a semester. Would an app like that get you looking up into the trees, or are you strictly a feeder-watcher?

A local boat captain's sonar picked up a mass of old tires strung together along the bottom of Cumberland Bay, estimated at 100 to 200 yards long and still unclaimed a month after he found it. What do you figure is actually down there?
Radio Bean, the North Winooski Avenue club Lee Anderson opened in 2000, closed its doors after a $29,000 insurance bill came due all at once. What's your clearest memory from inside that room?

Vermont Adaptive opened a new 27-foot yurt at Bolton Valley with a big deck and an accessible ramp, built for athletes with disabilities and named for the late donor who funded it, Douglas Taff. What sport would you want to try there first?

The Peace & Justice Center hid 33 clusters of tiny blue peace-sign stickers across 24 Burlington parks, with clues written as poems — so far exactly one person has found every single one. Which park would you start your hunt in?

UVM researchers helped map the genomes of eight bat species and found Vermont's own little brown bat, which can live 40 years or more, carries extra copies of the genes that hunt down damaged cells — a lifespan one scientist compares to a human living a thousand years. What animal fact has stuck with you the longest?

Loon nesting pairs in Vermont have climbed from about 15 in the 1990s to 115 last year, with two chicks hatching this summer on a volunteer-watched raft at Hinesburg's Lake Iroquois. Which Vermont lake would you bet on for your best shot at spotting one?

Those browning, crinkled sugar maple leaves you might've noticed are tar spot fungus — it exploded this wet summer but doesn't actually hurt the trees, and foliage is still on track to be dazzling. Which drive are you already plotting for peak color?

Crews pulled two derelict dams out of the Brewster River in Jeffersonville, reconnecting about 10 miles of trout habitat — the older one, a 50-foot timber crib dam from the late 1800s, once powered the mill that supplied a lot of the lumber Burlington was built with. What's the most surprising piece of local history you've stumbled into?

Colchester's Exit 16 is now running Vermont's first ever diverging diamond interchange, a design so rare only about 200 exist nationwide. Have you tried the new left-turn pattern yet, or are you still routing around it?

Lauren Gitlin retired her 53-goat milking herd at Villa Villekulla Farm in Barnard and is turning the place into a nonprofit offering animal-assisted therapy instead. Would a session with a goat actually calm you down, or just make you laugh?

The Venetian name goes back to 1917, when Justin Bunnell's great-great-grandfather started making ginger ale in the same Soda Plant building — now Bunnell is moving to Orlando and selling both the lounge and the brand. What Burlington spot's name would you most want to see carried on by someone new?

UVM's new Food Systems Research Station at Nordic Farm is putting GPS collars on cows to track which forage they prefer, with the team describing its job as making mistakes so farmers don't have to. What's one mistake you wish someone else had made first?

The Harborvale on Cherry Street rings a brass bell at the bar every night at sunset, and chef Doug Paine built the whole menu around nostalgia, from pork belly with violet mustard to bucatini with vodka sauce. What's the nostalgic dish you'd want on a menu like that?

Vermont orchards just launched a digital passport for apple season — scan a QR code at more than a dozen stops and each stamp enters you to win up to $500. Which orchard are you making your first stop?

South Burlington's Cathy Seward has volunteered at Burlington's King Street Center since 2009, and the New England Patriots Foundation just handed the center $10,000 in her name. What cause would you want to see get a surprise windfall like that?
The Grey Jay, the Honey Road team's breakfast and lunch spot on Pearl Street, closes for good after service on October 12th. What's the dish you're making sure you order again before then?

VTrans listed a 359-foot, 1928 bridge over the Winooski River on Vermont's Craigslist free stuff page, since federal rules require offering historic bridges away before replacing them — so far the only reply asked, 'Can I move it tomorrow?' What would you actually do with a free 359-foot bridge?

Scientists at the Vermont Center for Ecostudies are gluing solar-powered trackers, with names like Ann, Scott and Pam, onto monarch butterflies and following them in real time — some are turning up wintering in Florida instead of Mexico. Which butterfly name would you want to root for on the trip south?

A flock of sheep escaped from the Episcopal Diocese down the street and took a field trip across the grounds of the new Burlington High School before staff rounded them up. Where do you think they were trying to get to?

Crews just started ripping out the 60-year-old wooden grandstand benches at the Champlain Valley Expo — by next summer every seat gets its own spot and a cup holder. Which seat are you claiming at the fair next year?

Desmond Tse wore the same pair of Darn Tough socks for 101 days straight without washing them, smashing the old record of 55, and swears the merino wool never stank. How many days do you think you'd last?

Chapin Orchard in Essex Junction banks on roughly eight good weekend days each fall to make its whole pick-your-own season — on one recent Sunday when rain never showed, they still did half of Saturday's business. Which weekend are you circling to go?
